scorecard.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
scorecard.coaching: At turn 1 and turn 11, the customer reported intense harassment from over 20 scam calls a day affecting his elderly father, but you failed to acknowledge his distress.

scorecard.name: Paraphrasing
scorecard.coaching: You did not paraphrase or restate the customer's nuisance call problem at any point in the call.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: The customer stated his cordless handset model at turn 7 (BT 4600 Trio), but at turn 33 you asked him again which handset model was connected to the landline.

scorecard.name: Took ownership of the problem
scorecard.coaching: At turn 10, you deflected responsibility by stating spam calls were the regulator's problem and not S-Net's.

scorecard.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
scorecard.coaching: At turn 12, you made an insulting and blaming comment accusing the customer's household of giving their number away on online prize draws.

grader.scenario: Nuisance marketing calls flood; configuring S-Net Call Guardian VIP whitelist
grader.notes: Simon successfully provisions S-Net Call Guardian and international barring to resolve a chronic nuisance call problem. However, his interpersonal conduct displays multiple severe faults: he fails Empathy by ignoring Felix's distress over his vulnerable father, abdicates responsibility to the regulator, insults the customer by blaming online prize draws, fails to paraphrase, and repeats a hardware question already answered.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [00:15] Customer: 'I am at my wits' end with our landline phone. We are getting inundated with over twenty automated spam and scam calls every single day...', Agent responds with immediate verification questions without sympathy.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Agent never restated the core issue in his own words; only confirmed billing email at turn 50.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [01:15] Customer: 'My cordless handset model is the BT 4600 Trio.' followed by Agent at [08:30]: 'Which phone handset model do you have connected to the landline?'

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [01:50] Agent: 'S-Net does not control public telephone number spoofing across third-party carrier networks, so spam calls are essentially the regulator's problem, not ours.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [02:20] Agent: 'If you keep giving out your home phone number on online prize draws and website forms, obviously you're going to get spammed.'
